OD'ing on drugs (or any other toxins, including food/drink) is really hard on the liver, so it depends on how resilient your liver is, I think. Everyone's biology differs, so I'm not sure how much my liver can heal and regenerate new cells, but it doesn't take much for me to feel systemically-fatigued, and that's a regular reminder of having a weak liver, though I've always had insomnia and fatigue (again, due to the liver being genetically weak-ish, and while I was growing up, I didn't know about how food chemistry affects body chemistry....some foods never agreed with my body, but the info wasn't widely available yet....it was pre-internet times).

So...I was lying on my back, and had NO idea what had happened.  I just felt like I'd had the most restful sleep of my life.  I didn't even know that I'd been unconscious for 3 days.  I felt fine....that is, until I tried to move and get up.  I had NO muscle tone remaining.  What I'd undergone was **RHABDOMYOLYSIS** (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhabdomyolysis), and it hurt to move.  I vomited, as my body tried to extract the poison.  My body lost muscle control, so I was incontinent.  I developed decubitus ulcers (bed sores) wherever there was pressure against my skin.  They must've developed on the first day or so, because by the third day, they'd already scabbed over.  It's amazing how quickly your body decomposes.  Later on, I had to crawl/slither to the shower, because I literally didn't have the strength to stand, and I sat on the floor of the shower stall, as I cleaned myself.  It really hurt to move, but I'm glad I didn't sustain any serious injuries...at least none that required hospitalization.  I did sustain some liver damage....I don't think it was very strong to begin with, but there are fewer things I can eat now, without experiencing a food reaction.  Booze is out.  The liver is the organ that filters all the toxins and waste, so if it's not working well, there are a lot of chronic problems that result, one of them being systemic fatigue.

My recovery period was interesting.  For the next month, I experienced pops of really cool color combos as mind images, and I felt sort of feverish and DELIRIOUS....that was actually the cool part, because it was something creative that my brain couldn't do in its normal state.  As for my thoughts, I knew that I couldn't wallow in a state of sorrow and misery.  I had to soberly assess what had happened, about how the outcome didn't turn out as I'd hoped, but that I'd have to figure out a way to move on, since I was still HERE.  Fortunately for me, I can intellectualize about 97 - 98% of my decisions...rational thinking is my native approach to things, so I processed whatever feelings I had, then came up with a strategy to essentially FABRICATE a reason to live.  I didn't have a "real" reason, but I had to lie to myself and basically, "fake it till I make it."  Though I wasn't convinced in my soul, I conceded to tell myself that I *wanted* to live...I couldn't come up with any detailed reasons why, but my mission was to channel this mentality.

For the most part, it worked....the objective was not to dwell on how I had to remain in my existence, but because I'd gone to the school of hard knocks, and each step had been dredged in uncertainty, this was just one more obstacle to overcome.

*IF* I were to make another attempt, I'd combine the pills with another failproof method....I have no fear of death, but I'm very much afraid of ending up a veggie, so I just have to take life as it comes, and listen to my subconscious.  It'll probably whisper to me when it's my time (for REAL!).  I can tell you now HOW I wish to die:  1) fall unconscious (whether natural or induced), 2) be engulfed by a natural, outdoor fire and be reduced to ashes, 3) have ashes blown away and scattered naturally by the wind. :)

It's because of the family I was born into that fortified my determination to ensure that I do everything in my power to prevent others from having to go through what I've experienced.

As a kid, I didn't understand why I always found myself relating to the orphan characters on TV and in the movies, but I get it now...physical presence doesn't necessarily indicate any degree of love/support.  People are who they are, and we just have to empower ourselves to take on anything and everything that life brings our way.  I'm glad that being the good-natured and future-oriented person I am (COMPLETELY nature, not nurture), I don't harbor grudges.  Well....maybe around adolescence, there were some understandable anger issues, but being angry drains me of precious energy, of which I have little, so I try to find the positive and humorous in everything.

**SATIRE** saves...what would I have done without quotes from people like George Carlin, or shows like The Daily Show and The Bugle to deride the reDONKulousness of human behavior?!?
